text:
oliver: quick heads-up — during the sustained-burst perf run I saw p95 jump ~2.1x and a handful of 10s CPU stalls from the continuous-batcher. link: https://perf.internal/runs/1758 (flame + spans)
mira: ugh. do you have a correlation with kv-cache hit rate? my gut says evictions + kernel selection thrash.
jun: checked the traces — lots of short-lived batches that then cause a different kernel to be picked mid-seq. KV hits drop ~18% at the same time.
sophie: that matches what I saw in the profile: frequent kernel swap calls in the runtime scheduler, and microbatches end up with different seq-lens so the kernel chooser flips.
oliver: exactly. hypothesis: sustained burst creates many small-ish requests that get coalesced into big batches but with heterogeneous seq lengths + cold KV => bad kernel decisions and larger memory working set => more evictions.
raj: proposal: "adaptive tapering holdback" heuristic. idea: after N batches accepted in window W, start decaying the target batch size by factor f per step (helps maintain more homogeneous batches) and bias admission toward KV-hit requests.
mira: love the name. how would config look? can we express as simple YAML + fallback to current policy?
jun: rough config snippet I sketched:
```yaml
batching:
  adaptive_taper:
    enabled: true
    burst_window_sec: 8
    burst_threshold_batches: 6
    decay_factor: 0.8   # multiply target_batch_tokens by this on each step
    min_target_tokens: 32
    kv_bias: 1.6        # multiplier to prioritize KV-hit lanes
    soft_429_threshold: 0.92  # probability threshold to start soft rejects
```
raj: soft_429_threshold is probabilistic. above it we soft-reject low-priority/no-cache requests with a small 429 payload that includes a hint to retry-after and a short-circuit suggestion.
sophie: add a "taper_cooldown" so we don't oscillate: taper_cooldown_sec: 30
oliver: we'll also add kernel-stability guard: if kernel-switches > X in last Y secs, temporarily lock kernel for in-flight batches to avoid thrash.
mira: can we test this in perf harness? i want A/B with 10% traffic on canary pool + synthetic sustained burst generator (mix of big and tiny seqs)
jun: yep, I pushed a patch to the experiment repo:
`git+ssh://git.internal/redwood/continuous-batcher-exps@taper-holdback`
deploy-bot: canary rollout started for service=continuous-batcher pool=canary pct=10 — rollback_on_alerts=true
raj: metrics to watch: p99 latency, p95 latency, KV hit rate, kernel-switch-rate, batch-size-variance, eviction-rate. alert thresholds preconfigured in the dashboard.
mira: small note: watch for downstream clients that assume consistent responses — soft 429 semantics must include structured JSON: {"retry_after_ms":..., "reason": "soft_backpressure"}
oliver: agree. logging: add a field `admit_hint` on spans (taper_step, kv_biased, soft_429) so we can filter traces.
sophie: if this reduces p95 even modestly it could reduce unit cost (fewer kernel thrash stalls). good ROI.
jun: i'll run a 6-hour soak on canary tonight and post results tomorrow morning. if we see oscillation we'll tune decay_factor and cooldown.
mira: action items: 1) jun run canary soak (6h) 2) oliver add kernel-lock guard PR 3) raj add soft-429 schema to client-docs 4) sophie add dashboards/alerts. I'll sync with product if canary is green.
oliver: thanks. quick note: config rollout should be low-risk — default off and gated by `adaptive_taper.enabled` so we can flip fast.
mira: ok closing loop here. ping me if any regressions pop up. :thumbsup:
